newsitem.title: BURMA: Buddhist monks demonstrate in Mandalay at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Buddhist monks demonstrate in Mandalay at weekend.

text.p: Buddhist monks demonstrated on Saturday in Burma's second city Mandalay, but the protests were quelled without incident, government sources said on Monday.
The sources said the demonstrations were sparked by rumours that a young Buddhist girl had been raped by Moslems.
No further details were available and spokesmen for the military government were not immediately available for comment.
A government source said officials were still looking into the protest. He said there was no shooting involved and there were no casualties.
"We have now succeeded in quelling the riots," he said.
Diplomats in Rangoon said they had not heard of the protests, but said it was not unlikely in this profoundly Buddhist nation.
"It sounds very plausible," one diplomat said.
Buddhist monks played a key role in national pro-democracy uprisings that began in 1988, when hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets to protest against the military regime.

At the time, prominent monks appeared on television and appealed to the public to stay calm and pursue their cause peacefully while at the same time urging military leaders to listen and not use force.

The demonstrations were eventually quashed by the current rulers, the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), in a bloody showdown that left thousands of people -- including monks -- dead or imprisoned.

After the major demonstrations were quashed, monks continued to be involved in the protests against the military, especially in Mandalay. Their protest tactics included a boycott on performing religious services for soldiers and their families.
Since then the Buddhist monks have been largely silenced, through fear and in part through offerings given to top monks by the generals in the SLORC.
But diplomats and analysts say there have been some signs recently of unrest among younger monks who want to see Burma return to democracy.
Opposition sources say support from monks would be crucial for major change to take place in Burma.
